required: Board manufacturer/revision, every used printed terminal and orientation; U1/U2 package-to-adapter map; correct links/regulator mode; maker schematics for DevKit, BTS, L298 and bucks.
acceptance: One-to-one E2 functional-port to actual printed terminal map, readable photos/datasheets. Unreadable/unmarked terminal remains unconnected.

required: Chemistry, cell count, charge/discharge limits, continuous/peak C and duration, condition, main/balance connector identification and manufacturer sense order; fault envelope from documented data, never a battery short test.
acceptance: P1, charger, contact/fuse voltage/current and sense wiring selected against actual pack limits, not nominal 11.1V alone.

when: D data first; H later approved isolated tests
required: For each M1-M7: part/rated voltage and permitted range, load/run current, start peak and duration, stall current and permitted duration, insulation/pigtail limits; conveyor voltage specifically. Use manufacturer data or separately approved low-energy characterization, never hand-held stalling.
acceptance: Voltage and RMS/run/start/stall envelopes fit motor, driver, connector and coordinated cutoff limits; missing current profile prevents final power selection.

when: D data / E selection; H later confirmation
required: M1+M2, M3+M4 and M5+M6 totals, simultaneous M7 demand; documented board derating, delivered motor voltage, diode capacity, ambient/case/heatsink temperatures and thermal path; start/stall clearing limits.
acceptance: All continuous/pulse/thermal/voltage limits met simultaneously with stated margin; L298 failing any limit triggers a reviewed replacement revision.

required: Each branch/pigtail material/size/connector rating, one-way route length, ambient/bundling, allowed voltage drop, start/fault I-squared-t and source DC interruption envelope; contactor main/inrush/break and coil voltage/current range across loaded pack.
acceptance: Fuse clearing precedes smallest protected lead/motor/driver allowable overload; voltage drop/temperature acceptable; contacts and holders documented for DC service. No guessed AWG or fuse amperage.

required: Record test-lead resistance; each external segment end-to-end ohms, neighboring-net isolation and polarity with intended sensitive electronics detached; inspect four existing bonds separately. Identify any semiconductor path in context.
acceptance: Expected path agrees with conductor/lead budget, no unintended cross-net link; lead-resistance-corrected values reviewed. Never megger connected electronics or meter resistance across a live battery.

required: Each buck output no-load/peak load, startup/turn-off peak, ripple, temperature and OVP/OCP/UV/power-good response over approved input range; raw and protected outputs separately, dummy loads first.
acceptance: 5.00V target; protected healthy envelope 4.75-5.25V or tighter actual part limits, rated peak load/heat, fail-open coil-permissive response verified. Scope fast peaks; do not intentionally expose MCU to a buck fault.

item: ECHO, enable, reset and partial power
required: Raw/divided/U2-output HIGH/LOW, overshoot, rise/fall rate under actual harness, MCU/logic rail order and backfeed, GPIO14 and all six enables through boot/reset/brownout, summed receiver loads.
acceptance: U2 input HIGH >=2.0V, LOW <=0.8V, 0-5.5V and <=10ns/V edges at specified VCC; GPIO levels within ESP32 limits; no unsafe EN pulse/backfeed or raw 5V GPIO path. Use isolated test fixtures before MCU attachment.

when: I only after release; repeat after H
required: K1 dropout/coil range, stop-contact continuity, enable fall, bus residual voltage/discharge, normal manual reset sequence, held-reset/weld limitations, suppression and worst braking/regeneration peak/energy.
acceptance: Physical S2 removes all motor power independently of firmware, opens enable and drives GPIO27 LOW; release alone with S3 released does not restart. Clamp/reservoir and discharge/stopping limits supported by reviewed data/traces.

required: Each motor direction and permitted low-energy current, paired run/starting profiles and heat, brush inward sweep/conveyor transport, sensor/crosstalk ranges, actual speed/stopping distance at worst intended floor/load and supervision envelope.
acceptance: Physical directions correct, currents/heat inside approved limits; no auto restart, safe distance margin and guards; controller/simulation results alone never satisfy these measurements.
